title: State-distinct coverage-constrained product-key granularity frontier
question: For the registered persistent-state retrieval workload, what is the minimum fraction of states reranked that preserves a preregistered capability-retention floor when downstream success is state-distinct?
hypothesis: Increasing factor granularity reduces candidate occupancy, while increasing factor beam recovers coverage. With a state-distinct downstream objective, the joint factor-size/beam surface should expose a measurable capability-compute frontier.

endpoints.name: capability_retention
endpoints.role: primary capability-constrained frontier endpoint, bounded to [0,1]

decision_rule.condition: At each M, identify configurations with pooled capability_retention >= 0.80 and report the minimum states_scored_over_M among them.
decision_rule.licenses: a registered capability-constrained frontier on the corrected state-distinct workload
decision_rule.does_not_license: a universal optimum, universal sublinear retrieval, or hardware wall-clock speedup

decision_rule.condition: Identify configurations whose pooled capability_retention >= 0.80 at every M in {128,256,512}, then report the lowest mean states_scored_over_M among those globally eligible configurations.
decision_rule.licenses: evidence that one fixed product-key configuration can preserve a fixed capability floor while executing a bounded fraction of the state population on this workload
decision_rule.does_not_license: general semantic addressing or a completed C5 proof

held_constant: same 48 training codes versus 16 held-out target codes
same task seed stream across arms
protocol_note: This experiment preserves the predecessor arm surface and capability floor. The downstream executor is replaced by a fixed state-distinct executor; this is a new registration, not a rewrite of the voided result.
